# GEO report: ledger-site **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 71/100, Good Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 16.3 ÷ 23 × 100 = 71. High = (16.3 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 71. The plumbing is mostly sound: `robots.txt` is valid, no crawler is blocked by accident, and the navigation uses real links. The losses come from a missing `lang` attribute, no `Sitemap:` line in `robots.txt`, missing canonicals, a `noindex` on a page you list in your sitemap, and a blog that only loads in the browser. I read these results from code. Nothing was measured on a live site. I sampled 5 routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs`, `/blog` and `/thank-you`. That is every route in the repo. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Tell crawlers where your sitemap is (GEO-011, 2 points lost) - **Why it matters:** `robots.txt` is the first file crawlers read. Without a `Sitemap:` line they have to find your page list some other way. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1-5` - **What the code says:** `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` with no `Sitemap:` line anywhere. The file `public/sitemap.xml` exists and is valid. - **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`. - **Score after this:** 80. ### 2. Declare the page language (GEO-012, 2 points lost) - **Why it matters:** the `lang` attribute tells machines and screen readers which language the page is in. Titles and descriptions are already present on every route. - **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:11` - **What the code says:** `` - **Size:** Small. Change it to ``, which matches `site.language` in `geo.config.json`. - **Score after this:** 80 alone. Together with item 1: 89. ### 3. Add a canonical link to every indexable page (GEO-015, about 1.3 points lost) - **Why it matters:** a canonical link says which address is the main one for a page. Only `/` and `/pricing` have one. - **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1` and `app/blog/page.tsx` (it has no metadata export at all) - **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };` - **Size:** Small. Add `alternates: { canonical: 'https://www.ledger.example/docs' }`. The blog is a client component, so its metadata must go in a server `layout.tsx` for that route. - **Score after this:** 77 alone. Together with items 1 and 2: 91. ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`, plain text with valid lines | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-2`; policy is `allow` | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`; 3 of 4 routes clear | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Problem | Not run | `/docs` and `/blog` have none; 1 of 3 indexable routes clear | | GEO-003 | Main content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:8`; 4 of 5 routes clear | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and is complete | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Sitemap exists and is discoverable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:1-5`, no `Sitemap:` line | | GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` are present | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11`, no `lang` | | GEO-016 | Key pages are reached through real links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:13` | | GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | Only `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:15`, which is fine | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Clear | Not run | Read `app/layout.tsx` and all pages. There are no images, and every link has text | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | | GEO-010 | `llms.txt` (informational, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | None present. That is fine | | GEO-102 | App structured data (informational, not scored) | Not applicable | Not run | Not an app | ## Other problems found - **Pricing is in your sitemap and navigation but marked `noindex`.** `app/pricing/page.tsx:1`: `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. Its canonical also points at a page that tells search engines to stay away. If pricing should be found, remove the `robots` setting. If it's deliberate, remove `/pricing` from `public/sitemap.xml:4` and the nav link doesn't need to change. ## Worth considering - **The blog promises posts but the page itself has none:** `app/blog/page.tsx:8`: `fetch('/api/posts')`. Fetching the posts on the server (an async server component) would put the titles in the HTML. Each post could also get its own page and address, since today each is only a title in an `
`. - **Docs promise setup help but give one sentence:** `app/docs/page.tsx:3`: `

Start by importing your bank feed.

`, under a description that says "How to set up Ledger." Real steps in text would give both people and machines something to quote. - **Pricing facts could be labelled:** `app/pricing/page.tsx:3`: `

Free for up to three people.

`. Only the free tier is stated, and nothing says what comes after it. Once plans are spelled out in text, structured data (JSON-LD) could label them. - **Home page is thin and links nowhere beyond the nav:** `app/page.tsx:4`: `Invoices, expenses and reports in one place.` Short paragraphs on each of those three, linking to docs, would show what the product does. - **Sitemap has no dates:** `public/sitemap.xml:3`: `https://www.ledger.example/`. Add `` once you have real modification dates. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. I suggest `geopilot logs `, which checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Real status codes and headers:** whether `/api/posts` works, and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` header is added outside the repo, needs a live check. - **GEO-003 on `/blog`:** the code shows the posts load only in the browser. A live check would confirm how much text crawlers actually receive. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find the site. `geo.config.json` says `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`. - The `GPTBot` block in `public/robots.txt:4-5` is a deliberate choice that matches `trainingCrawlers: "block"`. I did not count it. - `/thank-you` is deliberately `noindex` and isn't in the sitemap or nav, so it didn't count against GEO-014. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
